intent: A Sierra Ridge homeowner wants artificial turf, a pet area or a putting green. Where is turf allowed, who approves it, and what makes a lot qualify or not?
distinctValue: Sierra Ridge is governed by a metropolitan district that enforces the Declaration and publishes a specific turf rule in its Rules, Regulations & Guidelines (revised effective 1 January 2025): ARC approval first, back yards only, the back yard enclosed on all sides by a privacy fence, and the turf not visible from the street or any common area tract. The same rules limit lots that adjoin a park, school playground, open space, common area or internal path to 48-inch open 3-rail fencing on those lines (tapered/stepped down from any adjoining privacy run), ban double fencing and freeze builder perimeter fencing except for interior heavy-gauge wire, but carve out a case-by-case exception for fencing around hot tubs, animal enclosures or play areas — the page's sharpest local value for an open-space lot that wants a dog run or a putting-green enclosure. None of that fence detail, the ARC's own timetable (up to 30 days, deemed disapproved after 45, appeal within 45), the 200-sq-ft pet-enclosure cap, the 6-foot play-equipment setback, the landscaping deadline for new owners, or the district's own drainage-interference rule appears on the Stonegate (SVOA rear-yard 30% rule), Meridian (Design Control Committee) or Lone Tree (attached vs detached homes) pages. The general Douglas County swelling-soil point and the PWSD day-by-day watering schedule are not repeated here because they already run on the Meridian/Stonegate/Arvada/Roxborough and Parker/Lone Tree pages; this page instead uses the district's own drainage-interference clause and points the reader to PWSD's current rules rather than restating them.

sources.label: Sierra Ridge Metropolitan District: Rules, Regulations & Guidelines (PDF, 65 pages)
supports: Cover: "Duly Adopted and Approved October 9, 2014 / Revised August 6, 2020 / Revised Effective January 1, 2025"

"Approval is required prior to the installation of artificial turf. Artificial turf is only allowed in back yards. The back yard must be enclosed on all sides by a privacy fence and the turf must not be visible from the street or any common area tracts."
Introduction: the District "has been designated as the enforcement entity for the Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Sierra Ridge."

Introduction: "no interpretation of these Rules and Regulations, no approval, and no variance or waiver, is valid unless it is in writing duly authorized by the District. Anything claimed to have been said or given by the Board, the District, the District Manager, the Architectural Review Committee ("ARC"), or any committee(s), must be in writing in order to be valid and binding."

"The term "Improvements" means all exterior improvements ... dog runs, fences ... landscaping, hedges, windbreaks, plantings, trees, shrubs, flowers, vegetables, sod, gravel, groundcover, excavation and site work"

Submittal Procedure: "Plot plan showing the location of the improvement(s)." "Landscaping descriptions - identify trees, shrubs, mulch areas, flower beds, vegetable plots, and pathways, play equipment, etc."

"The ARC strives to respond to requests quickly, however, the Committee normally meets once per month at irregular intervals, and it may take up to 30 days after the submittal is received for a response to be sent to you."
"If you do not receive a written response within 45 days, the request is deemed DISAPPROVED."
"If a request is denied, you may appeal the decision of the ARC to the Board of Directors by submitting a written request through the management company within 45 days of denial."

"In addition to the required approvals by the Architectural Review Committee ... the construction ... of any Improvements shall also require the applicant to obtain the approval of all governmental entities with jurisdiction thereover ... issuance of building permit(s) by Douglas County, Colorado, if required, shall be a precondition to commencement of construction ... The ARC shall not review or approve any proposed Improvements for compliance with governmental requirements."
Fences/Gates: "Approval is required prior to installation for any type of fencing. No double fencing is permitted."

"Perimeter/OpenSpace fencing installed by the builder/developer may not be removed, changed, or modified except for the installation of 2"x4" heavy gauge wire. Heavy gauge wire must be professionally installed or installed properly by using the "stretch" method and be placed on the interior of the fencing."

"Six foot (6') solid Privacy style fencing - Solid privacy fencing, internal to a lot, may be installed provided such lot is not adjacent to or abutting next to a park, school playground, open space, common area, or internal bike/pedestrian path"

"48 inch (48") Open 3-Rail style fencing - Homes backing to or abutting, park, school playground, open space, common area, or internal bike/pedestrian path, may only install 48 inch (48") Open 3-Rail fencing along those lot lines"

Landscaping: "The landscape for the Streetscape (also referred to as the "Tree Lawn"), being the area between the curb and the front of the sidewalk, is the responsibility of the homeowner. With the prior approval of the ARC, owners may install native and naturalized plants to reduce water consumption and fertilizer use in the Tree Lawn. The landscape plans should be consistent with the District's Water Wise Gardens Guide"

"Landscaping shall be completed within six (6) months after initial conveyance of the property to the owner ... Should an extension be foreseen due to time of year, written notice must be made to the ARC prior to the 6 month expiration, at which time; the ARC will issue a new time requirement to the owner, but in no case later than 12 months after conveyance."
"When planning landscape improvements, considerations should be given to plant materials that do not require excessive moisture around foundations."
"All unimproved areas at the time of conveyance must be landscaped using at least 50% plant material (such as irrigated turf, shrubs, trees, or other planted material)."

"Approval is required: A. Landscape plans and designs must be submitted to the ARC. B. Retaining walls or grade changes. ... D. Has less than 50% sod in the "front" and/or "rear" yards. E. If the property is adjacent to open space (parks, common areas, etc.) or roadways."

Pet Enclosures & Houses: "Approval is required for all pet enclosures. Maximum size of pet enclosure is 200 square feet. No larger than 10' x 20'. Acceptable fencing material shall meet the existing District fencing detail." "Chicken wire and chain link material is NOT permitted anywhere in the community."
Play Equipment: "Approval is required prior to installation. This includes fort-style play structures, swing sets, climbing equipment, sport courts, putting greens, etc."
Play Equipment, continued: play equipment, putting greens included, "shall be in the back yard and must be a minimum of six feet (6') from any property line."
Fences/Gates, continued: "Limited use of fencing around hot tubs, animal enclosures, or play areas will be considered on a case-by-case basis."
Fences/Gates, continued: privacy fencing "must be tapered down (or 'stepped') to meet any existing open rail."
Drainage: "There shall be no interference with the established drainage pattern over any property within the Community except as approved in writing by the ARC."
Exhibit D (Landscaping): "All owners are required to have landscape plans approved."

sources.label: Sierra Ridge Metropolitan District: Overlapping Entities
supports: The list reads: "Sierra Ridge Metro District, Town of Parker, Douglas County Re-1 School District, Douglas County Government, South Metro Fire Rescue Fire Protection District, Parker Water & Sanitation District, ..."
The district site names no water provider elsewhere; this list is the only mention of a water utility.

sources.label: Parker Water & Sanitation District: Service Area Boundaries
supports: "Parker Water & Sanitation District serves customers in the Town of Parker and various other surrounding communities, including portions of Castle Pines and Lone Tree. However, not all residents of the Town of Parker are served by PWSD."
"If you are unsure based on the map below, please contact the Customer Care team at 303-841-4627 to confirm."

Sierra Ridge's own Overlapping Entities list names both "Town of Parker" and "Parker Water & Sanitation District" as separate entities; Sierra Ridge is an unincorporated community per the Wikipedia and district-rules sources, not inside the Town of Parker, so PWSD's Town-resident statement doesn't by itself confirm Sierra Ridge service.

"Homes ending in an EVEN number = SUNDAY, TUESDAY, THURSDAY. Homes ending in an ODD number = MONDAY, WEDNESDAY, SATURDAY"
"you need a permit to be exempt from the standard watering guidelines when establishing new sod."
"PWSD has partnered with the South Metro Water Supply Authority to offer $750 turf removal discounts to our customers through Resource Central."

sources.label: C.R.S. 37-60-126, current text (FindLaw)
supports: (11)(a)(I): "Any section of a restrictive covenant or of the declaration, bylaws, or rules and regulations of a common interest community, all as defined in section 38-33.3-103, and any rule or policy of a special district, as defined in section 32-1-103 (20), that prohibits or limits xeriscape, prohibits or limits the installation or use of drought-tolerant vegetative landscapes, requires cultivated vegetation to consist wholly or partially of turf grass, or prohibits the use of nonvegetative turf grass in the backyard of a residential property is hereby declared contrary to public policy and, on that basis, is unenforceable."
(11)(d)(II): "This subsection (11) supersedes a rule or policy of a special district, as defined in section 32-1-103(20), only in the case of a direct conflict."

Scope note: the rules cite their authority as a special district under 32-1-1001 and 32-1-1004(8)(a), C.R.S. Neither the statute nor the district says whether a privacy-fence and visibility condition is a direct conflict, so the page sends the reader to the district for a written position.
